questions: With 16 mm footprints and a 0.015 m spacing, is the signal still discriminative near the centre, or do the sensors saturate and blur the steering signal?
Does the 0.10 m wheel track with 0.6 kg mass give enough turn authority on the slalom, or does the robot now oscillate or overshoot?
Are line-loss events now confined to particular bends or tracks, and which ones?
Does the forward offset of 0.06 m cause any visible lag or oscillation at the controller level?

intent: Change the platform for a first finishing attempt: shorter wheel track (0.10 m) and lighter, shorter body (0.6 kg, 0.14 m) to raise turn rate and lower yaw inertia; sensors moved forward to y = 0.06 m for earlier bend anticipation; 16 mm footprints to widen the lateral range over which tape is seen. Expected: fewer off-track ends and higher progress on the slalom and s-bend, with the oval the most likely first completion.
learning: H1: iteration 0 failed on turn authority and lateral drift, not on sensor coverage, because max error reached the 0.06 m off-track limit. H2: a shorter wheel track and lower yaw inertia will let the robot follow tighter bends and reach the finish. H3: a larger footprint widens the tape-visible band and cuts line-loss events. Next race: if it still goes off track with max error near 0.06 m and progress is low, the controller gain (or the drivetrain's speed) is the bottleneck, and I will move back toward a wider track for stability. If it finishes some tracks, I will tune sensor span and offset next. Measurements requested: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort, controller_errors and noise_robustness, reported per track.
rationale: Iteration 0 raced 60 trials and none finished. All 60 ended off track, with mean progress of 0.23 on the oval, 0.14 on the s-bend and 0.10 on the slalom. Max error sat at 0.062 to 0.066 m, just over the off-track limit of 0.06 m, so the robot drifts off the tape before it covers much of the course. Line-loss events were 1 to 1.5 per run and steering oscillation was modest (about 0.13 to 0.15), so the problem looks more like insufficient turn authority or late anticipation than jitter. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which is 0.06 for any body width in range, so body width cannot help and I will leave it at 0.12. Geometry changes for this iteration: (1) wheel_track 0.12 to 0.10 m, which raises turn rate for the same wheel PWM difference; (2) mass 0.7 to 0.6 kg and body_length 0.16 to 0.14 m, which lower yaw inertia (mass times (L^2 + W^2)/12) so the robot turns faster; (3) sensor forward offset y 0.05 to 0.06 m, so the signal is read earlier on bends, as the Integrator's own note suggested; (4) sensor_size 0.012 to 0.016 m, which widens the lateral range over which each sensor sees partial tape (about ±0.0235 m instead of ±0.0185 m) and should reduce line-loss events. Expected result: fewer off-track ends, more progress on the slalom and s-bend, and possibly the first completions on the oval. Caveat: I changed several parameters at once, so if the result is mixed I cannot attribute it to a single cause. I accept that cost to get a finishing baseline quickly.
